content: Root cause: The bug was caused by race conditions occurring between concurrent write operations and IOCTL commands in the ALSA sequencer subsystem. Specifically, there was a lack of proper mutex protection around the whole write operation, which led to potential unexpected pool operations from another thread while one thread was either writing or performing an IOCTL. This could lead to undefined behavior, such as buffer overruns or memory corruption, when both operations accessed shared data structures simultaneously without appropriate locking mechanisms in place. The previous fix had addressed pool initialization races, but did not cover broader write operation protections, necessitating this patch.
